title: arXiv Biology and Biomedicine: Notable Recent Papers — Week of Nov 7–13, 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart or readership statistics; this inferred relevance ranking uses sparse attention signals and incomplete biomedical coverage. Most clinical and experimental biology preprints appear outside arXiv, especially on bioRxiv and medRxiv. This is not a comprehensive biomedical survey or clinical guidance.

sections.title: Headline
sections.summary: Ten notable papers from Nov 7–13 center on protein-interaction models and experimental validation, with a second strand in single-cell genomics and benchmark quality. Agenda: what new molecular models actually validate, and where biological evaluation can still mislead. The ranking is inferred; arXiv has no official trending chart and its biomedical coverage is incomplete.

sections.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
sections.abstract: Bonbon learns protein–ligand interaction representations and reports zero-shot mechanism, binding-site, and bond-type predictions, followed by prospective compound testing.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a 3.2-trillion-token paired-sequence model, scaling tests across 42M–1.6B parameters, and a prospective 61.5% dose-response hit rate across nine disease targets in seven protein families.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say reported capabilities are coarse-grained and do not produce explicit 3D coordinates; the prospective hit rate is not clinical evidence, and model weights/data are not openly released.

sections.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
sections.abstract: ProTEUS combines sequence, evolutionary, and structural representations with iterative experimental feedback to select higher-order protein variants.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report two closed-loop enzyme campaigns: 90 levansucrase variants over three rounds yielded a 14.03× wild-type screening-activity variant; 150 aldehyde-dehydrogenase variants over five rounds yielded a 6.85× screening-activity variant (7.90× after catalytic-rate normalization).
sections.unique_caveat: Experimental evidence is limited to two enzyme targets and modest campaign sizes; activity gains do not establish transfer to other proteins or applications.

sections.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
sections.abstract: Pyrite tests whether LLM agents can rank difficult protein–ligand poses more accurately than expert chemists using structured geometry and interaction features.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report up to 67% accuracy for direct LLM ranking and 74% for LLM-guided feature construction plus logistic regression, on a 1,500-pair benchmark spanning 285 structures and 1,799 poses.
sections.unique_caveat: Poses originate from the authors' proprietary co-folding/sampling system; model-agent performance is computational pose ranking, not evidence that a drug binds or works in a patient. The paper notes a remaining accuracy gap and possible distribution shift.

sections.title: scBIG++: Learning Across Genes and Cells to Predict Single-Cell Perturbation Responses
sections.abstract: scBIG++ predicts heterogeneous single-cell responses across all retained protein-coding genes rather than restricting inference to highly variable genes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce expression-adaptive gene modules and population-conditioned generation to reconstruct perturbation responses over 6,539–19,451 genes, reporting benchmark recovery under unseen targets/combinations and held-out compounds.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are benchmark-based predictions from existing single-cell perturbation data; they do not establish that predicted responses occur in newly performed experiments or in human patients.

sections.title: When gene summaries reveal the answers: Gene Ontology circularity in gene embedding benchmarks
sections.abstract: This study measures how generated gene summaries can expose Gene Ontology labels to text-embedding benchmarks and proposes provenance-aware comparisons.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors found Alliance-generated summaries for 6,172 human genes (32.1%). Removing them reduced reported per-gene AUROC by 0.078 for a linear probe among genes with 1–10 linked publications; the effect also appeared with other encoders and text sources.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors flag a historical GO scorer that mishandled ties, and original predictions were unavailable for rescoring; the reported effect size is therefore provisional. Shared curation sources also complicate interpreting a benchmark as pure leakage.

sections.title: Pruning DNA Sequence
sections.abstract: Sequence Pruning dynamically removes genomic sequences that become easy to predict during DNA-language-model pretraining.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report up to 96% less data processing while largely retaining downstream performance; at the most aggressive setting, training used 4% of baseline GPU hours with little performance loss.
sections.unique_caveat: These are benchmark- and corpus-specific computational results. The paper does not show that the same savings preserve performance for every genome, task, or pretraining distribution.

sections.title: OriDynamics: Towards a World Model for Biomolecular Dynamics
sections.abstract: OriDynamics generates all-atom conformational ensembles for proteins and complexes while modeling coordinated fluctuations between interacting partners.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine latent-space conformational exploration with local all-atom sampling and ensemble-level supervision of mean positions, fluctuation amplitudes, and coordinate covariance; benchmark results claim better conformational coverage, fluctuation fidelity, and interaction geometry than selected baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is computational benchmark and application analysis, not a demonstration that generated ensembles reproduce experimentally measured dynamics across diverse systems.

sections.title: The DynaCell Evaluation Suite for Dynamic 3D Virtual Staining of Live Cells
sections.abstract: DynaCell evaluates virtual fluorescence staining on 3D live-cell time series using pixel, organelle-segmentation, and single-cell-phenotype measures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors find regression baselines better for localizing target organelles, while a generative baseline better captures phenotype distributions across cells, across three cell types, two microscopes, four organelles, and three perturbation states.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an evaluation suite, not evidence that virtual staining is interchangeable with fluorescence for every cell type, microscope, or downstream biological conclusion.

sections.title: KineCouple: Substrate-conditioned residual readout for enzyme kinetic prediction
sections.abstract: KineCouple uses substrate-conditioned attention over protein residues to predict enzyme kcat and Km from sequence and substrate representations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report small gains over a reproduced CataPro baseline: kcat RMSE 1.333 to 1.330 and PCC 0.492 to 0.496; Km RMSE 0.998 to 0.997 and PCC 0.633 to 0.634.
sections.unique_caveat: Improvements are numerically modest and computational; kinetic predictions complement, but do not replace, experimental enzyme characterization. No independent biochemical validation is reported in the abstract.

sections.title: PathwayDesigner: an interactive SBML/KEGG/Reactome/Escher compatible editor for biochemical network diagrams
sections.abstract: PathwayDesigner is an open-source editor for biochemical network diagrams that supports several pathway formats and computes stoichiometric network summaries.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author presents a cross-platform Rust/WebAssembly editor that imports/exports SBML and related maps, preserves model components, annotates species and reactions, and visualizes stoichiometry, conservation laws, and flux null spaces.
sections.unique_caveat: Passing file round-trip and interoperability tests is software validation, not evidence that downstream pathway models or biological interpretations are correct.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: Recurring evidence spans protein interaction/structure modeling, single-cell perturbation and genomic-model evaluation, plus data provenance, benchmark design, and file interoperability. These are patterns in the selected corpus, not a claim of field-wide change.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: Follow-up directions include preregistered assays across more protein families for Bonbon and ProTEUS, independent pose generators and temporal/scaffold splits for Pyrite, and corrected-scoring reruns with provenance tracking for GeneProv. Replicate scBIG++ and DNA-sequence pruning on external datasets under fixed compute budgets; compare OriDynamics to experimental ensembles; test KineCouple on external kinetic data; and test DynaCell across independent labs and microscopes.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: This week's clearest pattern is a cluster of protein-modeling work that ranges from sequence-only interaction predictions to closed-loop enzyme evolution. Several papers make evaluation itself the contribution. The strongest translational evidence remains early wet-lab validation in a small number of targets; most results are benchmark-based, not clinical evidence.
